# Incident Report: MTA-2024-08-15 Traffic Analysis

## Evidence Reviewed
- `2024-08-15-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (18,189 packets). No separate IDS/Suricata alert exports were present in the evidence directory; all findings below are derived directly from packet content via tshark.

## Victim Host
| Attribute | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **10.8.15.133** | DHCP lease, HTTP/DNS traffic |
| MAC address | **00:1c:bf:03:54:82** (Intel NIC) | DHCP Discover/Request frames |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-H8ALZBV** | DHCP option 12, NBNS, mDNS, mult. DNS self-queries |
| AD domain | LAFONTAINEBLEU (lafontainebleu.org), DC at 10.8.15.4 | NBNS, LDAP/Kerberos/CLDAP traffic |
| Logged-in user | **plucero** | Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS-REQ CNameString field, seen from 10.8.15.133 to DC 10.8.15.4 |

## Malware Family
**GootLoader** (JS-based initial-access/dropper malware, distributed via fake-download landing pages) — **behaviorally attributed**, not signature/AV-confirmed (no AV/YARA verdict artifact was provided in this evidence set). Confidence is high based on the distinctive, well-documented delivery chain:

- The lure was a fake FedEx tracking/"quote" page (`quote.checkfedexexp.com`) that served a ZIP disguised as a shipment/invoice document.
- Inside the ZIP was `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js` — a **6,990,020-byte JavaScript file** (SHA256 `dab98819d1d7677a60f5d06be210d45b74ae5fd8cf0c24ec1b3766e25ce6dc2c`) padded almost entirely with unrelated filler text lifted from public documents/books (MPI standard docs, IPCC reports, OECD survey text, etc.) around 731 `eval(` calls and a `WScript` reference. This "giant JS bloated with irrelevant scraped text to evade size/AV heuristics" packaging is a hallmark GootLoader technique.
- This JS stage then pulled a second-stage payload — a Windows PE32+ DLL, `0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` (SHA256 `b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6`), 159,232 bytes — from a hardcoded IP over plain HTTP (BITS/7.8 user agent), which is consistent with GootLoader's follow-on loader stage.
- Following the DLL retrieval, the host immediately began persistent, unsolicited outbound beaconing (`GET /` and `POST /` every few seconds, spoofing an old `MSIE 6.0` user agent) to the same raw IP on port 80 — consistent with a loader/C2 check-in loop. The specific C2 malware family behind this beacon (e.g., a Cobalt Strike-style stager or custom loader) could not be confirmed from network metadata alone; that portion of the attribution is **behavioral/uncertain**, not signature-confirmed.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 / malicious infrastructure**
- `72.5.43.29:80` — hardcoded IP, DLL payload host and post-infection beacon C2 (no DNS lookup preceded contact — IP was hardcoded in the JS/loader)

**Malicious domains**
- `quote.checkfedexexp.com` (resolved to 104.21.55.70 / 172.67.170.159, Cloudflare-fronted) — initial lure/delivery domain
- `business.checkfedexexp.com` (same resolved IPs) — same phishing infrastructure, queried by the host but not observed serving a payload in this capture

**Malicious URL**
- `http://quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?16553a25e45250a41fd5&endeds=MIGpq&JStx=59bf050d37df88a9-ade43358-eaa1220b-0571422b-0f33e6aa150e86bafd0ed4&Ld=9d7502d88d752a27b1d00587309184b5a215` — served the malicious ZIP (`application/octet-stream`, 200 OK)
- `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` — served the second-stage DLL (mislabeled `text/html`, 159,232 bytes)

**Transferred files / hashes**
| File | Size | SHA256 |
|---|---|---|
| `managements` (ZIP archive, delivered as query-string filename) | 2,767,804 bytes | `798563fcf7600f7ef1a35996291a9dfb5f9902733404dd499e2e736ea1dc6fc5` |
| `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js` (inside ZIP) | 6,990,020 bytes | `dab98819d1d7677a60f5d06be210d45b74ae5fd8cf0c24ec1b3766e25ce6dc2c` |
| `0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` (PE32+ DLL, x86-64) | 159,232 bytes | `b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6` |

**Timeline (all times UTC+4, as in the pcap):**
1. 04:10:58 — GET to `quote.checkfedexexp.com` triggers ZIP download (received 04:11:04)
2. 04:11:59 — HEAD/GET of DLL from `72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7...` (159,232 bytes)
3. 04:13:00 onward — repeated `GET /` and `POST /` beacon traffic to `72.5.43.29:80` with spoofed `MSIE 6.0` user agent, mostly answered with HTTP 400 by the C2 server, continuing at the point traffic capture was examined

## Recommendation
Isolate DESKTOP-H8ALZBV (10.8.15.133) from the network immediately, reset credentials for user `plucero` and any accounts used interactively on that host, and block `72.5.43.29`, `quote.checkfedexexp.com`, and `business.checkfedexexp.com` at the perimeter/DNS layer pending full disk forensics.
